findings.title: The new overload replaces the existing four-dimension downsize API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by arity. Defining `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` here replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition, rather than adding a second accepted signature. Any existing caller using the formerly supported width/height form will now raise `ArgumentError` (five arguments supplied to a method accepting three or four), breaking thumbnail/image-processing callers outside this diff.

findings.title: Five fixed 80% reductions cannot ensure the upload meets the configured maximum
findings.body: The reduction loop is capped at five iterations and each iteration only reduces dimensions to 80%, so a 10 MiB image is still roughly 3.3 MiB after all five attempts (and may compress even less effectively depending on image contents). Sites configured with a lower `max_image_size_kb` will still have the upload rejected by `Upload.create_for`, despite this path claiming to automatically reduce images to the allowed size. The resize ratio/iteration strategy needs to be based on the configured target or continue until the target is reached with a safe termination condition.

findings.title: Client-side validation now ignores both configured image and attachment limits
findings.body: Replacing `max_<type>_size_kb` with a hard-coded 10 MiB limit means attachments are now accepted by the browser even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is much smaller, only to fail on the server later. It also prevents clients from uploading images above 10 MiB when an administrator has configured a larger image limit. The larger pre-processing allowance should be limited to images that can actually be downsized; attachments must continue to use their configured limit.
